fr.elements: Main Residence; Access Drive; Detached Structure; Open Green Space; Dense Vegetation; Landscaped Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to define the access point during nighttime or low-visibility conditions.
• Trim trees and shrubs along both sides of the driveway so emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and debris so responding units can reach the residence without delay.
• Clear a turnaround area near the residence or detached structure large enough for a fire engine or ambulance to reverse direction without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Cut back dense vegetation where it meets the driveway edges to prevent it from narrowing the usable travel width for large vehicles.
• Keep a gate or barrier at the driveway entrance unlocked or equipped with a Knox Box so responders can enter without delay.
• Mark the detached structure with a visible identifier so responding crews can distinguish it from the main residence when staging or searching the property.
• Thin dense vegetation between the main residence and detached structure to give responders a clear path between the two buildings.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Scattered Shrubs; Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Mixed Vegetation; Grass Cover; Open Terrain; Single Access Route; Long Driveway; Limited Rear Access; Scattered Trees; Adequate Vegetation Separation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin scattered trees nearest to the structure to increase open space between the tree canopy and the building.
• Trim shrubs growing close to the structure's exterior walls and foundation.
• Cut or mow grass cover in the immediate area around the structure to reduce low-level fire spread toward the building.
• Remove any shrubs or small trees growing directly against the structure.
• Separate clusters of shrubs from one another by removing or thinning vegetation between groupings near the structure.
• Keep the full length of the driveway clear of overhanging branches so emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Trim trees and shrubs along both sides of the driveway to maintain a clear travel lane.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is visible to emergency responders approaching from the road.
• Clear vegetation from the rear of the structure to allow movement and access around the building.
• Mow or cut grass along the driveway edges to reduce the path by which fire could travel toward the structure.
• Remove dead branches from trees near the structure, particularly on the sides facing heaviest vegetation.
• Keep the area immediately surrounding any outbuildings or improvements clear of shrubs and tall grass.
